doc.title: Bob Stewart interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006

title: Grandparents in AME ministry, Newport and first trumpet
summary: He lived with his minister grandparents, moved to Newport, listened to the Newport Jazz Festival, and began trumpet in 1956.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: But my father moving around a lot, so I lived with my grandparents, my mother’s parents, Reverend and Mrs. Simmons. And he was an AME, African Methodist Episcopal minister. And more often than not you didn’t stay longer than seven years in any place. So at that time we were in New York City up at 116th and Madison at Mt. Zion AME church. It’s still there as a matter of fact. And by 1953 we moved to Newport, Rhode Island.

Quite a change. And it just happened to be the home of the Newport Jazz Festival at the time and I used to ride around Freebody Park and listen to the music on my bicycle. I couldn’t find any money to get in so I would just listen. And Mahalia Jackson stayed at our house around 1958, ’59 and sang at our church on Sunday morning and it was wonderful. But it was in 1956 I started playing trumpet in the elementary school, fourth or sixth grade, one or the other, and that was my first instrument.
Some music teacher along the way said I need a tuba player?
